question: How many 'red alert' dengue clusters (10+ cases) will Singapore's NEA list as active on 29 October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Latest NEA snapshot (16 Oct) per Little Big Red Dot shows 3 Red clusters: Ho Ching (95 total, 4 in last 2 weeks), Bishan St 12 (16, 5), Lentor Gdns/Tung Po (12, 9). The automated page readings disagreed on the Red labels, which adds some uncertainty. Weekly cases are falling (79, then a partial 49) at the end of peak season, so Ho Ching may go Green. Lentor and Bishan are still active, and a new Red cluster in 13 days is possible but unlikely (the other clusters have at most 4 cases). No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers. Median 3, skewed slightly down.

calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: 2 vs 3 Red as of 16 Oct. All runs report Lentor Gdns/Tung Po at 12 cases, which is Red under NEA's 10+ rule; Little Big Red Dot (cited by Runs 1 and 2) and Run 3's page read say 3 Red. The figure of 2 comes from the 12 Oct weekly update, before Lentor crossed 10. Settled as 3, with a small residual for the conflicting automated label reads. How fast clusters close (14 vs 21 days) could not be verified without web access, so I treated Ho Ching and Bishan drop-outs as about 25% each. The judgment calls (how many close vs how many new Reds) give a median of about 2.8, slightly below the 3.0 of Runs 1 and 3, because two of the three incumbents have only 4-5 recent cases and the season is waning. Agree with the runs' reference-class framing. No markets found by the runs; none searched this run.
